contradictions.quote_a: Electric pallet jacks, hand pallet jacks, stretch wrappers and the cardboard baler require instruction, not manager authorisation.
contradictions.quote_b: the 8 electric pallet jacks or the 12 hand pallet jacks without individual authorisation by the Warehouse Manager.
contradictions.explanation: One section states electric and hand pallet jacks need only instruction and explicitly not manager authorisation, while the other requires individual Warehouse Manager authorisation for the same equipment.

contradictions.quote_a: They run on the 4.0 m main transport aisles and never enter the 3.0 m high-bay aisles for high lifting.
contradictions.quote_b: Counterbalance forklifts shall not be used for high-level put-away or retrieval in the high bays except where the maintenance technician and shift supervisor have expressly confirmed suitability
contradictions.explanation: One section imposes an absolute ban on counterbalance forklifts entering high-bay aisles, while the other permits their use there when suitability is confirmed.

contradictions.quote_a: Only wrapped and labelled pallets enter Zone D.
contradictions.quote_b: (a) scanner-verified picking in Zone C, (b) labelling and transfer to Zone D, (c) wrapping, (d) staging by outbound door
contradictions.explanation: One section requires pallets to be already wrapped before entering Zone D, while the other orders transfer to Zone D before wrapping.

contradictions.quote_a: pick faces in Zone C are never supplied from Zone F.
contradictions.quote_b: operators place to Zone B, Zone E or Zone C feed only by task.
contradictions.explanation: One section forbids ever supplying Zone C pick faces from Zone F, while the other directs operators in Zone F to place restocked goods to Zone C feed.

violations.quote: the 10 km/h indoor limit with 5 km/h at meeting points
violations.explanation: The fact requires 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, not at meeting points.
